result.instructions: Tools for Waitwhile, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Who is waiting in line at my shop right now?"; "What bookings do I have tomorrow, and for which customers?"; "How many visits did we have last week, bookings and walk-ins?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Waitwhile data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run waitwhile_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run waitwhile_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run waitwhile_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. waitwhile_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: List the account's locations (businesses/sites): id, name, short name, address, time zone, opening hours and waitlist/booking settings. Use the ids to filter visits, services and resources. GET /locations.

external_id.description: Only the location with this external id.

start_after.description: Cursor: pass the previous reply's next_start_after to get the next page.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_location
tools.title: Get location
tools.description: One location by id or short name (the part of its public Waitwhile URL). GET /locations/{shortNameOrId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_location_status
tools.title: List location status (live waitlist)
tools.description: Live status of every location: open/closed, number of people waiting and being served, current estimated wait time, and booking counters. GET /location-status.

start_after.description: Cursor: pass the previous reply's next_start_after to get the next page.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_location_status
tools.title: Get location status (live waitlist)
tools.description: Live status of one location: open/closed, waiting and serving counts, estimated wait. GET /location-status/{locationId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_visits
tools.title: List visits (waitlist entries and bookings)
tools.description: List visits: waitlist entries (people in line) and bookings (appointments), with customer, state (PENDING, DRAFT, BOOKED, WAITING, SERVING, COMPLETE), tags (e.g. NO-SHOW, CANCELLED, ARRIVED), services, resources, party size, position and timestamps. Filter by location, state, tag, customer, service, resource, booking date (local time) or created/updated date. Cursor-paged. Contains customer contact details. GET /visits.

from_booking_date.description: Bookings starting at or after this local date-time, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm.

to_booking_date.description: Bookings starting at or before this local date-time, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm.

from_date.description: Visits created from this date-time (ISO 8601 or epoch ms).

to_date.description: Visits created up to this date-time (ISO 8601 or epoch ms).

start_after.description: Cursor: pass the previous reply's next_start_after to get the next page.

tools.name: waitwhile_search_visits
tools.title: Search visits
tools.description: Search visits by a prefix match on customer name, phone, e-mail or customer id, optionally filtered by location, state, tag and excluded tags. Page-numbered. Contains customer contact details. GET /visits/search.

q.description: Prefix match on name, phone, e-mail or customer id.

exclude_tags.description: Leave out visits carrying any of these tags.

page.description: Page number, from 1 (default 1). Pass the previous reply's next_page.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_visit
tools.title: Get visit
tools.description: One visit (waitlist entry or booking) by id: customer, state, tags, services, resources, party size, position, estimated wait and all timestamps. GET /visits/{visitId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_booking_slots
tools.title: List booking slots
tools.description: Booking slots of a location for a date range with the free spots per resource and service, so you can see when an appointment can be booked. Dates are local to the location, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm. GET /visits/availability.

service_duration.description: Service duration in seconds, to size the slots.

show_min_spots.description: Only slots with at least this many free spots.

tools.name: waitwhile_first_available_slots
tools.title: First available booking slots
tools.description: The first available booking slots of a location (optionally for a party size, services and resources) from a date. Use it to propose appointment times. GET /visits/first-available-slots.

max_num_slots.description: Max number of slots to return.

tools.name: waitwhile_create_visit
tools.title: Add a customer to the waitlist or create a booking
tools.description: WRITE: create ONE visit at a location. Without a date it adds the customer to the waitlist; with a local date-time (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm) it creates a booking. Needs a location and at least a name, phone or e-mail. Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two visits. Visit notes are not supported here (the field is deprecated): use waitwhile_add_customer_note. By default the request asks Waitwhile to suppress the customer message; this may only stop the immediate confirmation, and scheduled reminders/follow-ups can still go out per the location's settings. With send_notifications=true Waitwhile may text/e-mail this ONE customer. POST /visits.

date.description: Booking start in the location's local time, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm. Omit to join the waitlist.

send_notifications.description: Default false: the request asks Waitwhile not to send the immediate confirmation/status message. This may not stop everything: scheduled reminders and follow-ups can still go out according to the location's own settings. Set true to let Waitwhile send its normal messages to the customer.

tools.name: waitwhile_update_visit
tools.title: Update a visit (state, tags, time, party)
tools.description: WRITE: change ONE visit — its state (e.g. WAITING to SERVING to COMPLETE, or BOOKED), add/remove tags (e.g. ARRIVED, CONFIRMED, NO-SHOW), booking date/duration or party size. Only the fields you pass change. By default the request asks Waitwhile to suppress the customer message; this may only stop the immediate status message, and scheduled reminders/follow-ups can still go out per the location's settings. With send_notifications=true Waitwhile may text/e-mail this ONE customer. Use waitwhile_cancel_visit to cancel. POST /visits/{visitId}.

date.description: New booking start, local time YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm.

send_notifications.description: Default false: the request asks Waitwhile not to send the immediate confirmation/status message. This may not stop everything: scheduled reminders and follow-ups can still go out according to the location's own settings. Set true to let Waitwhile send its normal messages to the customer.

tools.name: waitwhile_cancel_visit
tools.title: Cancel a visit
tools.description: WRITE: cancel ONE visit (a waitlist entry or booking). Waitwhile sets its state to COMPLETE and adds the CANCELLED tag; the visit is kept, not deleted. By default the request asks Waitwhile to suppress the customer message; this may only stop the immediate cancellation notice, and scheduled reminders/follow-ups can still go out per the location's settings. With send_notifications=true Waitwhile may text/e-mail this ONE customer. POST /visits/{visitId}/cancel.

send_notifications.description: Default false: the request asks Waitwhile not to send the immediate confirmation/status message. This may not stop everything: scheduled reminders and follow-ups can still go out according to the location's own settings. Set true to let Waitwhile send its normal messages to the customer.

tools.name: waitwhile_add_customer_note
tools.title: Add a customer note
tools.description: WRITE: add one staff note to a customer's record (optionally tied to a visit and location). Adds only; nothing is edited or sent to the customer. POST /customers/{customerId}/notes.
